articles.title: X-Men Actor Christopher Abbott Insists His Professor X Is Not in Doomsday or Secret Wars
articles.summary: Professor X actor Christopher Abbott said Marvel fans won't see him in Avengers: Doomsday or Secret Wars because he needs to wrap up his time with X-Men before doing any cameos. The Marvel Cinematic Universe newcomer tried his best not to play coy during a conversation with Rolling Stone.
body: "I don't think so," when asked if he'll appear in any cameo roles before X-Men. "I don't even know… See, what's happening? What do you mean?"

Christopher Abbott, who will play Professor X in 2028's ‘X-Men’ reboot, says he will not be in the upcoming Avengers movie. “I don't think so. Well, I don't even know–what's happening? What do you mean? I don't know what's going on. On no. I'm not in that. I gotta do the ‘X-Men’ movie first before any of that stuff.”
When the interviewer clarified, asking if he'll play in Doomsday, he had a quick reply: "No, I'm not in that."

Abbott joined a cast of other would-be mutant heroes when Marvel Studios confirmed he had been picked to play Professor X at D23 earlier this year. The announcement also came with a May 2028 release date, giving him plenty of time to prepare to play the group's leader, and if fans are lucky, show up for a scene or two beforehand.

articles.title: Mass Effect Leaks Reveal Canceled BioWare Game's Story Would Have Accounted for 'All' Choices From Previous Games
articles.summary: Additional details about BioWare's canceled Mass Effect game have leaked online, revealing a story that would have taken choices from the Commander Shepard trilogy into account if EA hadn't shut down the studio.
body: The long-awaited and currently canned follow-up for the sci-fi RPG franchise, which was working under the title Mass Effect: Universe, was built around decisions made in the original games, according to comments shared by former technical director Romain Toutain during a recent livestream (via Kotaku ). As more details about the project leak, there's no telling exactly how thorough this system would have been, but he did his best to give fans an idea.

"All the choices made in the first Mass Effect games were taken into account," Toutain said (translation via Bluesky user @loustica-lucia.bsky.social ). "One of the reasons why it was called 'Mass Effect: Universe' is that you had so many choices. That you could plug your saves together to create parallel universes, to keep it simple. It's not exactly how it worked. You had different timelines, basically."

articles.title: Sydney Sweeney's New Netflix Sci-Fi Space Epic Gets First Details
articles.summary: The live-action Gundam film has been in the works in some form or another since 2018. A director and cast have been announced, including high-profile names like Sydney Sweeney joining the project.
body: Now one of the movie's stars is pulling back the curtain ever so slightly.

Appearing on the Happy Sad Confused podcast this summer, Gundam and Street Fighter star Noah Centineo revealed the movie is a "big action romance space movie." Centineo continued by describing Gundam as, "a non-Shakespearean Romeo and Juliet in space." That is a bit of a confusing statement, but what I think Centineo means is that the film is about star-crossed lovers on the opposite sides of a generational conflict. That sounds like it could fit perfectly within established Mobile Suit Gundam lore, as the series often focuses on the war between the Earth Federation and the Principality of Zeon in the Universal Century timeline.

As shifting allegiances and a growing threat set them on a collision course for one another, they’re pulled into a high-stakes race across the stars that could define the fate of humanity. With awe-inspiring battles, intimate human emotion, and an epic cinematic scale, this is Gundam like it’s been seen before.

articles.title: Mass Effect Universe Director Reveals Canceled Game's Multiverse System
articles.summary: BioWare's technical director reveals that Mass Effect Universe was set to feature a complex parallel-universe system with multiple timelines.
body: BioWare's canceled Mass Effect game would have been more than just one "universe."

Romain Toutain, Mass Effect technical director at BioWare since 2022, went live on Twitch on Saturday, where he watched the leaked trailer for the next installment in the Mass Effect series, Mass Effect Universe. Toutain discussed lore, gameplay, and technical details, revealing new details about the scrapped sequel. It was a bittersweet moment, as the game that could have been sounds like it would have exceeded the community's high expectations.

In terms of lore, Toutain confirms that the bartender in the trailer is a new alien race. He describes the organic, Reaper-like being as hairy and reveals that it might have been able to grow more tentacles. While analyzing the strange creature, the new Quarian companion shows the N7 protagonist its bioscanner data page. Unfortunately, Toutain was unable to tell us more because, just like the writers formerly working on the project, there is information that remains confidential.
points: BioWare's technical director reveals that Mass Effect Universe was set to feature a complex parallel-universe system with multiple timelines.
BioWare's canceled Mass Effect game would have been more than just one "universe."

articles.title: Clayface Looks Like a Win for the DCU After Earning $43 Million in Box Office Opening Weekend
articles.summary: Clayface looks set up to be a win for the DCU after securing the top spot at the box office with an estimated global haul of $43 million.
body: It's a strong start for the low-budget DCU film, split between $24 million domestically and $19 million internationally. The opening weekend total falls toward the higher end of early projections as audiences showed up to see Tom Rhys Harries bring a twisted and often overlooked Batman villain to the big screen.

With brutal body horror elements in a story that sees the birth of its titular character, Clayface follows Matt Hagen as he attempts to rebuild his life after a horrible attack leaves his face scarred. Starring Harries, directed by James Watkins, and written by Mike Flanagan and Hossein Amini, this latest DCU movie took viewers into the darkest corners of James Gunn and Peter Safran's universe they've seen yet, with a pretty hard-R rating.

It's for these reasons that the DCU's foray into a new live-action Gotham City left fans with question marks as they feared how a more adult-oriented story could fit into the same world as something as bubbly and bright as 2025's Superman. So far, at least, it seems to have paid off, at least compared to Supergirl, which landed as a dud in the DCU earlier this year.

articles.title: Tomb Raider's 2027's Return Looks Stunning in New Official Footage
articles.summary: The original Tomb Raider game celebrated its 30th anniversary this weekend, marking the 3D platforming adventure's release on Sega Saturn — yes, it came to Sega's doomed 3D console before its PlayStation and PC release a month later.
body: Released this weekend at the TR30 Derby and MCM London, the latest sneak peek at the Tomb Raider remake is full of nostalgic moments made even more spectacular — or at least much more graphically realistic.

The latest look at Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis showcases the game's four major locations — Peru, Greece, Egypt, and Atlantis — and some of their most memorable moments. That includes the giant Atlas puzzle, the monstrous Atlanteans that Lara has to fight, and the unfortunate consequence of stepping on the hand of King Midas' statue. If you have been curious about what a cursed, golden Lara looks like with modern technology, look no further.

While much of what's on display is classic Lara Croft, including the incredible acrobatics she employs during gunfights, Crystal Dynamics and Flying Wild Hog aren't doing a one-to-one remake with Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis. The remake will include plenty of gameplay modernizations too, such as a "Focus" meter, skill trees, and crafting.

articles.title: Rumored Lucia Actress Goes Viral After Dodging Swarm of GTA 6 Comments During Livestream
articles.summary: Manni L. Perez, the actress long rumored to be playing Lucia in GTA 6, has gone viral after dodging a swarm of comments from Grand Theft Auto fans during a recent livestream.
body: Rockstar Games has refrained from confirming the vast majority of the cast of next month's new GTA game, but as if there was ever any doubt, that hasn't stopped ravenous fans from piecing a list together themselves. Perez is one name theorists have talked about for years, so she took a few minutes to let thousands of viewers get to know her while masterfully dodging a swarm of GTA 6 comments along the way.

Reaching a peak of more than 2,100 viewers on a six-month-old Instagram account with just nine posts, Perez spent her 12-minute livestream just talking about her life growing up in a "small, rural, redneck-y" town. She lives in a studio apartment with a dog, loves to cook, grew up driving trucks, and as far as everyone else is officially concerned, she definitely will not be the star of the so-called biggest video game of all time in a little less than a month.

articles.title: 15 Years Later, Batman: Arkham City Remains Batman's Last Gaming Masterpiece
articles.summary: Batman: Arkham Asylum was released in 2009 at a time when superhero video games were usually relegated to being uninspired movie tie-ins. Some of them were good, like X-Men Origins: Wolverine, but most of them were either forgettable or downright bad.
body: Rocksteady’s Batman: Arkham City came out on Oct. 18, 2011. 15 years later, it’s still considered one of the best games around, and its influence can still be seen in other superhero games. It’s also undoubtedly the last universally beloved Batman game.

Compared to Arkham Asylum, Arkham City opens things up. Instead of being confined to the creepy corridors of the psychiatric hospital like in the first game, a whole section of Gotham becomes Batman’s playground for brutally maiming criminals within an inch of their lives. Random enemy encounters, fun one-off boss battles, and countless collectibles — so many goddamn Riddler trophies — populate its world. With all these elements, Rocksteady basically created a playbook for future superhero games, like Insomniac’s Spider-Man series, to successfully copy.

articles.title: Call of Duty movie will explore the "cost of war", says director
articles.summary: The Call of Duty movie will explore "the cost of war" and probably won't be as graphically violent as director Peter Berg's upcoming Netflix film, The Mosquito Bowl.
body: In an interview with ComicBook, Berg, who is directing from a script by Taylor Sheridan, said the Modern Warfare games the film draws on are about more than shooting.

Berg said that underneath the hardware and killing, the games are "really looking at the cost of war, the cost of having to be a warrior who's, for whatever reason, chosen to put himself between real danger and the rest of us, and the burden that these guys carry".
He described the characters - Captain Price, Soap, Ghost, and Alex - as "complicated humans", not "cartoon characters or comic books", and said there's "a real soul" beneath the violence.

"This is not just 'Hey, let's shoot them all up and shoot popcorn!' Like, there's a soul underneath it, that I understand that Taylor Sheridan understands, and I think probably not quite as graphically violent as Mosquito Bowl, but there will be a very strong soul, and consequence of war within the film, called 'duty,'" he said.
points: The Call of Duty movie will explore "the cost of war" and probably won't be as graphically violent as director Peter Berg's upcoming Netflix film, The Mosquito Bowl.

articles.title: Elden Ring movie has a budget of nearly $200 million
articles.summary: A24's live-action Elden Ring movie is reportedly set to cost almost $200 million, making it the most expensive film the studio has ever made.
body: The figure comes from a new report in the Wall Street Journal, and suggests there's been a big jump from earlier reports in April, which then put the budget at "well over" $100 million.
For context, A24's priciest film to date, Marty Supreme, reportedly cost around $70 million, a step up from Alex Garland's Civil War at about $50 million.
The WSJ's piece is less about Elden Ring than about A24's growing clout in Hollywood and the rivals now chasing its success.
"They're a Goldilocks company. Just the right amount of people doing just the right amount of things," Telluride Film Festival director Julie Huntsinger told the paper (thanks, IG ).

articles.title: Commander Shepard actors Jennifer Hale & Mark Meer mourn BioWare: 'It was in the hands of ownership that may not have understood what BioWare fully is''
articles.summary: As reported by IGN, veteran actors Jennifer Hale and Mark Meer, who voiced the female and male Commanders Shepard in Mass Effect, respectively, directly addressed fans of the series in an October 21 Instagram Live. The two reflected on BioWare, and commiserated over its tragic fate.
body: Both actors' reactions strike me as so characteristic of their respective backgrounds: Hale is one of the voices of videogames (not to diminish Meer's own extensive resume). She jumped to BioWare's place in the industry and its current crisis. Meer, a standby of the Edmonton theater and improv scene, fixated on the closure's effects on this city he clearly loves.
Both are 100% correct about the collective joy and meaning people found in BioWare's work. That's something private equity can't take from us ⁠—at least not with current technology.

As for Hale's optimism regarding the rights and potential future of the franchise, well, I Want To Believe. Not to obnoxiously needle what seemed like an offhand idea, but I don't think Kickstarter's walking through that door. Aside from Double Fine's Broken Age and the utterly baffling case of Star Citizen, many gaming crowdfunding successes⁠—like Pillars of Eternity and Wasteland 2⁠—still required further, traditional investment to go gold. BioWare and/or its IP would be orders of magnitude more expensive.

articles.title: 187K+ fans call for EA to "Save Mass Effect"
articles.summary: A petition created to save BioWare's well-loved sci-fi RPG, Mass Effect, has topped 187,000 signatures.
body: We said a sad farewell to BioWare earlier this week. Job cuts, coming just months after Saudi Arabia's $55bn leveraged buyout of the company, were anticipated by experts, but drew widespread condemnation and messages of sympathy from across the industry.

Joe Smith, credited with starting the petition, isn't necessarily asking EA to change its mind about BioWare; instead, the petition calls for "decisive action by committing to the continued development of Mass Effect".
"This commitment requires proper funding, adequate staffing, and time allocation to maintain and advance the high standards the franchise is known for," the Change.Org page reads.
"Alternatively, EA could consider licensing the Mass Effect intellectual property (IP) to another studio that shares the passion and vision to keep it alive and allow it to flourish anew."

articles.title: Indies and non-sequels have exploded in the last year, and it's not all friendslop
articles.summary: You'll never play every game. In fact, most people won't play most games—plenty of games release on Steam to approximately 0 user reviews, and last year, more than half of the 19,000 games that came out had fewer than 10.
body: That insight comes courtesy of Sensor Tower (via GamesIndustry.biz ), which recently published an industry analysis report sharing some trends among the year's breakout hits. For reference, a breakout is defined in the study as a game which sold at least 500,000 units in its first 30 days. While ultimately based on estimates as not all publishers release sales numbers, the report is full of interesting tidbits.

The most noteworthy findings in the report are thus: there were 76 breakouts between September 2025 and August 2026, up from the previous year's 55. Indie breakouts shot up from 13 to 33, making up 43% of the pack, and 35 of the breakouts were non-sequels—around 53%. 27 of those were made by indie studios. Nine of the indie breakouts were friendslop hits like Meccha Chameleon and RV There Yet?, while 18 were debuts in other genres, such as Escape From Duckov and Megabonk.
points: In fact, most people won't play most games—plenty of games release on Steam to approximately 0 user reviews, and last year, more than half of the 19,000 games that came out had fewer than 10.

articles.summary: Last week, the other shoe dropped for legendary RPG studio BioWare: shortly after EA's acquisition by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund and investment firms Silver Lake and Affinity Partners, the gaming giant shut down BioWare and canceled Mass Effect 5.
body: Fans have spent the intervening days combing through the detritus of the next game in the series' leaked remains, and some have even signed a change.org petition to save the series. Right now, that #SaveMassEffect petition has hit over 180,000 verified signatures.

Notably it does not call for EA to walk back its decision to shut down BioWare. Instead, it's about keeping the Mass Effect series going: "We are urgently petitioning EA to take decisive action by committing to the continued development of Mass Effect," Joe Smith's plea reads. "Alternatively, EA could consider licensing the Mass Effect intellectual property to another studio that shares the passion and vision to keep it alive and allow it to flourish anew."

articles.title: An officially licensed Knightmare game, based on the British TV show, is coming next year
articles.summary: A free point-and-click adventure based on Knightmare, the cult ITV children's show, is in development.
body: For the uninitiated, Knightmare aired on ITV between 1987 and 1994 and single-handedly introduced an entire generation of kids to fantasy RPGs and computer games. Sitting with Treguard, the deeply affable Dungeon Master, three kids in ironed jeans and their best button-up shirts would direct a fourth member of their team, the Dungeoneer, through a labyrinthine hand-painted dungeon, solving riddles, casting spells, and - hopefully - avoiding traps.
Interestingly, the players' life force meter - the stuff of legend of (k)nightmare fuel - has been ditched in a bid to give players the time they need to explore.

Much of its cast is returning, including Hugo Myatt as Treguard, Mark Knight as Lord Fear, Clifford Barry as Brother Strange, Edmund Dehn as Gumboil the Knight, Iona Kennedy as Greystagg, and Paul Valentine and Alec Westwood as jesters Motley and Folly, respectively.
Watson says the game's art was drawn by hand, stressing "everything you see and hear is made by real humans" (thanks, VGC ).
